description: Barrowman's worked centre-of-pressure examples: printed inputs and printed results, in inches, as facts extracted from the scans. Checked by hpr_aero::tests::barrowman_worked_examples (M1.5a).

sources.naram8: J. S. and J. A. Barrowman, The Theoretical Prediction of the Center of Pressure, NARAM-8, 1966; refs/papers/barrowman-1966-naram8-nakka.pdf (PDF pages 45-49 hold printed pp. 41-45, PDF pages 52-55 hold pp. 47-50)
sources.tir33: J. S. Barrowman, Calculating the Center of Pressure of a Model Rocket, Centuri TIR-33, 1970; bound in refs/papers/barrowman-1966-naram8-nakka.pdf (printed page = PDF page - 79)

tolerance_reason: M1.5 done-when: CNα and CP reproduce Barrowman's worked examples within 1%. Printed values are hand or slide-rule results to three or four figures.

examples.source: naram8 pp. 41-45 (drawing p. 41; nose and fins p. 42; X_F and K p. 43; boattail p. 44; totals p. 45)
notes: The nose CP is 0.466 L (Barrowman's fit for ogives); hpr integrates the tangent ogive's volume.
The fin slope uses the mid-chord length 1.81 in; the geometry gives 1.803 in.
The boattail CP puts d1/d2 = 0.754 (aft over fore) into eq. 44, whose d1 is the fore diameter; fore over aft gives 0.655 in instead of 0.72 in.

examples.source: naram8 pp. 47-50 (configuration drawing p. 47; nose and fins p. 48; X_F and K p. 49; totals p. 50)
notes: The calculation keeps only the ogive nose and the sustainer's four fins; the booster, its fins and the blunted tip are left out, as here.
The fin slope uses a mid-chord length of 39.7 in 'found by measuring enlarged fin drawing'; the geometry gives 40.50 in.
p. 48 prints (1.509)^2 for (1.059)^2, and the total CP on p. 50 uses 425.45 in for the fins' 425.37 in.

examples.source: tir33 pp. 21-22 (drawing and fins p. 21; X_f and totals p. 22)
notes: The fin is idealized to a trapezoid by filling the corner at the back of its root (p. 21).
The fin slope uses the mid-chord length 1.7 in; the geometry gives 1.692 in.

examples.source: tir33 pp. 23-25 (drawings pp. 23-24; nose and shoulder p. 24; fins and totals p. 25)
examples.six_fin_rule: TIR-33 p. 25 scales six fins by N/2 with K_fb = 1 + 0.5 R/(S + R) and no fin-count factor. hpr uses the fin-count factor 0.913 from MIL-HDBK-762(MI) p. 5-24 with K = 1 + R/(S + R) (ADR-008). The slopes marked six_fin_rule are checked with TIR-33's rule substituted, and hpr's own values are checked to differ from them by exactly the ratio of the two rules.
notes: The nose is idealized as a cone 4.15 in long whose imaginary tip is 0.8 in ahead of the real tip (p. 24): station_offset_in is added to every printed station to place the parts, and subtracted from every computed CP.
The fin drawing (p. 24, Fig. 16) gives a tip chord of 0.85 in; the calculation (p. 25) uses 0.8 in, which produced the printed results.
The fin slope uses the mid-chord length 1.64 in; the geometry gives 1.631 in.

examples.source: tir33 pp. 27-29 (drawing p. 27; fins p. 28; totals p. 29)
notes: The sustainer ends at the sustainer fins' trailing edge (20.0 in) and the booster at its fins' trailing edge (24.0 in); tube lengths don't enter Barrowman's slopes.
The mid-chord lengths are 2.25 in and 3.45 in; the geometry gives 2.241 in and 3.45 in.
The sustainer-alone CP, 17.9 in, comes from rounded moments (575/32.2 = 17.86).
